name: src/game/runtime.js
summary: The whole tuned game — sim, audio, music, render, HUD, storage — is one 12,335-line function body between the @runtime-body markers.
detail: Owns everything the player experiences; the TypeScript around it owns only the frame loop, input normalisation, textures and lifecycle. Called by src/scenes/CosmoScene.ts through the object returned at 12329-12335. It must never import from src/ — the VM harnesses evaluate the marker-delimited body standalone, so a bare import breaks every check. Read db/notes/code/runtime-regions.md before slicing it.

name: runtime host adapter
summary: Normalises the optional Phaser host into runtimeHost and wraps every addEventListener so runtimeDestroy can unsubscribe all of them.
detail: Owns runtimeHost, gameHaptic, runtimeListen, and the pointer/key event normalisers that turn Phaser events into DOM-shaped ones. Everything in the file that binds a listener goes through runtimeListen; the array it fills (17) is drained by runtimeDestroy (12309). It must not read gameplay state and must never throw when the host omits a field — a missing haptic or canvas is normal, not an error.

name: canvas, context and in-app-browser sniff
summary: Resolves the 2D canvas and context from the host or from #c, and decides IN_APP_BROWSER for the iOS audio-gesture hint.
detail: Owns cv, ctx, IN_APP_BROWSER and safeEl (the CSS safe-area probe read by resize). Everything that draws uses this one ctx; there is no second canvas except the host-supplied WebGL background. It must not size the canvas when runtimeHost.externalLoop is set — Phaser's Scale Manager owns the backing store there (see resize at 615-618).

name: BUILD stamp and freshCheck
summary: Stamps the deploy commit into the page and, once, redirects a stale cached title screen to the newest build.
detail: Owns BUILD (73), window.COSMO_BUILD (74) and freshCheck (93-108). freshCheck is called once at 12326 on the no-host path only; it is disarmed for BUILD==='dev', for a URL already carrying ?u=, and for any state other than the menu. It must never block boot: every failure path is silence.

name: COL and the written house style
summary: Declares the closed colour vocabulary (one colour per meaning) plus TAU, rand, RM and LAP_EMB_MAX.
detail: Owns COL (119-127), the reduced-motion flag RM (111) used as a guard by roughly forty draw sites, and LAP_EMB_MAX=4 (161). The house-style comment at 128-160 is the file's only statement of its naming rules: one name per thing, "NOUN xN" for multipliers and "NOUN . N" for counts, one colour per meaning. Nothing may add a colour here without a meaning nothing above already owns; red is reserved for death alone.

name: arena constants and the ring table
summary: Declares the elliptical arena dials, the live RADII stack (three rings, four inside a black hole) and RINGS, the per-ring instrument table.
detail: Owns ARENA_STRETCH/ARENA_MAX_Y (178-179), the screen globals W H DPR cx cy R AY u safeTop safeBot (181), RAD_OFF/RAD_BH/RAD_BAKE/RADII (204-207) and RINGS (210-224). RADII is live and eased by bhTick (2343), never a constant. RINGS carries wave/cut/lift/sub/tint, read by musicStep, bedTick, performerHit and the rail draw. Nothing may store a per-object radius: radiusOf(s.ring) is the only radius an ember has (see the warning at 676-687).

name: sky bands and the eight worlds
summary: Declares SKY_BANDS (four palette bands keyed to the tier ladder), WORLDS (eight procedural destinations), the orbit-to-world exchange rate and SKY_ARENA_CALM.
detail: Owns SPR/sprU..sprBand (242-243), SKY_BANDS (251-259), skyI (260), WORLDS (265-301), ORB_PER_WORLD/ORB_WORLD_SECS (303), LEVEL_HOME (325) and SKY_ARENA_CALM (328). skyI is written by startGame and by the tier ratchet in update, clamped to 3; WORLDS rows are interpolated by skyMix and uploaded as shader uniforms. It must not read G — the first sprite bake runs before G exists.

name: buildSprites and the SPR cache
summary: Bakes sixteen canvas sprites once per real resize so no draw pass pays shadowBlur per frame — but only five of the sixteen are ever blitted.
detail: Owns makeCanvas (329, dead), buildStarField/starField (339-351, dead), makeSprite (352), blit (362) and buildSprites (372-605). Called only from resize (655) and only when u, DPR, W, H or skyI changed; buildSprites(true) is a no-op because scene colour is procedural now. The shard, orb, shieldRing, mote, pip and shock bakes have no reader — artifactSprite replaced them; see db/notes/code/dead-bakes.md before tuning anything in here.

name: resize()
summary: Recomputes DPR, W/H, cx/cy, the scale unit u, safe-area insets, the arena box (R and AY) and re-bakes sprites when the size or sky band moved.
detail: The single owner of every screen-derived global. Called by the host through the returned resize, by the window listener at 665 when there is no host, once at 666, and from runtimeStep (12217) and frame (12241) when skyI changes. It must not touch the canvas backing store when runtimeHost.externalLoop is set, and it deliberately does not call glResize — glRender does that every frame.

name: posAt, the parallax dolly and ring radii
summary: Converts (angle, radius) to screen space including the camera-dolly offset, so every object on an orbit gets the same parallax as its track.
detail: Owns angDist, ringOf, radiusOf, ARENA_PARALLAX/PARA_K, paX/paY, depthOf, posAt, ecx and ecy. paX/paY are written once per frame in draw (10696) from camX/camY; every position in the game flows through posAt so nothing can come unstuck from its ring. It must stay a pure function of radius — a per-object stored offset is the detached-glow bug class documented at 676-687.

name: buildBus and the fixed WebAudio graph
summary: Builds the one-time bus — world / bed-duck / hole / pump / band / perf into limiter, makeup, soft clip — that every voice in the game routes through.
detail: Owns AC, muted, audioUnlocked, A, MASTER (739) and buildBus (744-825). Called from ensureAudio (2867) and defensively from beep (2924) and soundImpact (2568). A.hole and A.pump have exactly one writer each by discipline; A.perf bypasses both so the player's own instrument survives the drop. Nothing may add a second duck on A.hole without writing its own undo in the same call.

name: the arrangement tables
summary: Declares the tempo grid, the live chord/arp tables, the payoff hook tables and the queues the visuals read.
detail: Owns BPM/SPB/STEPS (847), CH and ARP (848-855) which applySect overwrites per section, STARRUN (864), LAYER_AT/LAYER_NAME (870-871), PAY/S16/PAYLEN/PAYREST (894), HOOKL/HOOKBL/HOOKGL/HOOKBGL/ANSWERL (914-1014) and MU/NOISE/BEATQ/LOOPQ. CH and ARP are the LIVE tables — every reader (pad retune, chTone, basslines) sees the current section by construction. LOOPQ (1019) is inert: nothing schedules it.

name: buildBed and MU
summary: Creates the four continuously running pad voices, the noise buffer every hat reuses, and MU — the single mutable object holding all music-scheduler state.
detail: Owns BED (826 declared, built here) and MU (1051-1076). The pad is retuned, never restarted, so bar seams do not click. MU's fields are the whole scheduler contract: step/next/chord, sect/sectAt, pay/payEnd, armed/rise/pend, brk, glow, orbitTone. Called once from buildBus (824). bedTick is the only writer of BED.g — a second writer is the stuck-pad bug.

name: the synthesis voices
summary: One function per instrument — note, hat, kick, snare, bassN, swellPad, riser, lead, gtr — plus subF, the 40 Hz octave-doubling guard.
detail: Owns subF (1078), note (1082), hat (1106), kick (1134), snare (1154), bassN (1161), swellPad (1173), riser (1194), lead (1211), DIST (1220) and gtr (1223). Every one early-returns on muted or a missing bus, so a silent run costs nothing to play. Called from musicStep, payoffStep, bhStep, finStep, breakStep and the cue helpers. They must never read G directly — pitch comes in as an argument so the level key transposes by construction.

name: the starfall build meter
summary: Counts star-fed orbits toward Starfall — and rejects every other source, which is why BUILD_SRC, DROP_STEP and the four-way meter described in the comments are dead.
detail: Owns DROPQ (1263), BUILD_SRC (1288, unread), DROP_STEP/DROP_STEP_MAX (1314, both 0), dropNeed (1315), starfallActive (1316) and build (1317-1326). build() returns immediately unless src==="orbit" AND amount>=0.04, so the only surviving caller is the completed-fed-orbit site at 8404 — the ember, hop, time and near-miss calls are all no-ops. dropNeed is 3, or 2 with the hairtrig upgrade.

name: the Starfall reward
summary: Three waves of guaranteed stars flying in from the world's planet, with invulnerability for the whole PAYLEN section.
detail: Owns tryLand (1328, an empty retired stub still called from four input sites), starfallWave (1329), startStarfall (1350) and tickStarfall (1360). startStarfall fires a nova blast, sets G.invuln to cover PAYLEN+0.6s and pulses the scene; tickStarfall is driven from updateOrbMotion (5915). Each wave now carries a flight path from the planet's limb (1336-1345) rendered by starfallFlightPos. It must not run inside a black hole.

name: armDrop and the (unreachable) pre-drop hush
summary: Arms or banks an earned Starfall and plays its two-note stab; the hush automation beside it has no caller.
detail: Owns armDrop (1372-1402) and schedulePreDrop (1403-1427). armDrop banks into MU.pend whenever a section, rise or cooldown is in flight, so an earning is never discarded. schedulePreDrop has ZERO call sites — MU.hushEnd and MU.lpLock are only ever set to 0, so duckBed's hush guard (2846) never trips and bedTick's lpLock guard (2837) always passes. Do not tune the hush curve expecting to hear it.

name: fireDrop and payoffStep
summary: The eight-bar payoff: one impact, then an authored hook whose bars 2, 3 and 6 are the band answering itself.
detail: Owns fireDrop (1428-1478) and payoffStep (1479-1543). musicStep hands off to payoffStep whenever MU.pay>0 (1721) and calls fireDrop on an armed even eighth (1725). MU.crown (the ring the drop fired from) sets richness, never payout; MU.flavor colours the section. It must not schedule its own kick at t — the caller runs payoffStep at the same t and bar 0 fires one.

name: endSection and fireLift
summary: The one path that clears any interrupted musical phrase, banks an unpaid earning, and restores every automated gain.
detail: Owns endSection (1544-1577) and fireLift (1578-1593). endSection has thirteen call sites — mute, death, pause, visibility change, black-hole entry, level change, musicTick's stall detector — and is the belt-and-braces restore for A.hole and A.pump. It always lands back on the verse (applySect(0)). fireLift is the 2.3s tier-unlock fanfare and is deliberately not a chorus.

name: breakStep
summary: One authored bar of descending tom fill, transposed into the level key by kf, that never remaps an input.
detail: Owns breakStep. Called only from musicStep (1806) while MU.brk counts down from 8; the crash that brings the record back belongs to musicStep (1810). The figure is written in A minor and multiplied by CH[0][0]/110, so level 1 is bit-identical.

name: powerColour, orbitMusicState and orbitColour
summary: Turns the live orbit — its fill fraction, streak, last turn and last hop — into a shared state object that colours both the pad and the sky.
detail: Owns powerColour (1612), orbitMusicState (1625) and orbitColour (1638). orbitMusicState reads G.currentFlow (the dust-wake envelopes) and is consumed by musicStep (1796) and bedTick (2733); orbitColour plays at most two quiet notes per orbit, on quarter slots only, memoised in MU.orbitTone. It goes inactive during hypernova, overdrive, a payoff, a black hole and the finale so it can never double a fanfare.

name: musicStep
summary: The 585-line arrangement: section handoffs, the chord retune, every layer gate, per-level basslines and kits, and the hypernova star run.
detail: Owns musicStep (1652-2236), chI (2237) and chTone (2238). Called only from musicTick, once per eighth on the audio clock. Order is load-bearing: the pad retune sits above every return so the pad tracks the progression while ducked; then black hole, then payoff, then armed-fire, then the star dive, then the ordinary arrangement. The rise branch is unreachable — line 1727 pins rn=-1 and rise=false.

name: PLAY, LOOP and FIN
summary: Declares the player-as-performer state, the inert legacy recorder, and the star-dive finale object.
detail: Owns PLAY (2243: heat, idx, last, slot, bias, biasN, tape), LOOP (2246, inert) and FIN (2262-2263). PLAY.bias is the learned device latency, persisted across runs within a session and slewed at most 3ms per tap after twelve gated samples. PLAY.tape and LOOP are retired recorder storage kept only so the cleanup paths still have something to clear.

name: the black hole mode
summary: A seventeen-second optional wager that re-spaces the arena to four rings, drags the comet inward, and pays on an escape to the outer ring at twelve seconds.
detail: Owns BH_DUR..BH_HORIZON (2270-2277), bhDensity, BH, bhActive, bhTick (2285), startBlackHole (2344), endBlackHole (2373) and bhStep (2405). bhTick is called from update whenever the state is playing OR the mode is active, so it can finish across a death; it is the only writer of RADII (2343). It outranks everything in musicStep including a payoff already in flight, and it must withdraw every entity from ring 3 before that radius closes (2317-2328).

name: finStep
summary: The star dive's own eight-eighth kit, thickening with FIN.voices and FIN.got as the melody is gathered.
detail: Owns finStep. Called from musicStep (1741) once FIN.on and the latch bar has passed. Voices are added at every fourth star; the harmony is the level verse, re-retuned in place at the latch so the dive never plays over a chorus chord.

name: gridNear, CUE and cueTone
summary: Lands every game reply on the nearest sixteenth, one voice per slot, so a burst of pickups comes out as an actual note run.
detail: Owns gridNear (2474) and CUE/cueTone (2494-2495). cueTone has twenty-four call sites — embers, orbits, shields, hops, cues, milestones, the finale. gridNear returns the grid point itself, which can sit in the past; callers clamp. A taken slot cascades by one sixteenth, capped a beat out. It must not return a fresh timestamp per call or performerHit's one-note-per-slot dedupe stops working.

name: gridOff and judgeTiming
summary: Scores a tap against the quarter and the sixteenth relative to a learned per-device bias, climbing the ON BEAT chain only on the quarter.
detail: Owns TIGHT (2545), gridOff (2551) and judgeTiming (2562-2676). Called only from performerHit. Three tiers: CLIMB (tight against the quarter) raises the chain and pays; HOLD (sixteenth only) refreshes the decay but never climbs; a miss costs one link and never the chain and never points. The bias EMA takes twelve fast samples then slews at most 0.003s per tap inside +/-0.12.

name: performerHit
summary: Turns every tap and hop into a chord tone of the bar on the player's own bus, panned by the wake's direction.
detail: Owns performerHit. Called from reverseFX (6598), hop twice (6961, 7013) and nothing else. It walks an inline figure — [0,2,1,3,2,0,3,1] for a tap, a direction-dependent four-cell for a hop — transposed by ring, resolved against the sounding chord by chTone. One note per sixteenth slot: the PLAY.slot dedupe at 2680 is what stops held-key auto-repeat stacking notes.

name: musicTick
summary: The 160 ms lookahead loop that walks MU.step forward on the audio clock, capped at sixteen steps per call.
detail: Owns musicTick. Called only from the bottom of bedTick (2839), so it inherits update's frame cadence but schedules on AC.currentTime. A gap of more than 0.4s abandons the section rather than replaying it compressed — that one line covers every stall path including a backgrounded tab and a pause.

name: bedTick and duckBed
summary: The only writer of BED.g and the pad voice weights: level, cutoff, band gain, the payoff pull-back and the starfall queue drain.
detail: Owns bedTick (2728-2840) and duckBed (2841-2851). Called unconditionally from update (7789) so it catches every stall path musicTick bails out of. It redistributes the pad's fixed 0.16 budget between root/octave and third/fifth from orbitMusicState.pressure (2734-2739), sets the filter cutoff from clock, heat, groove, ring, section and orbit, and drains DROPQ into startStarfall. A second writer of BED.g is the stuck-pad bug this file has shipped twice.

name: ensureAudio, visibility and mute
summary: Creates and unlocks the AudioContext inside a gesture, abandons a section across a background, and gates the bus rather than the clock on mute.
detail: Owns ensureAudio (2852), runtimeVisibilityChanged (2872) and toggleMute (2900). ensureAudio is called at the top of pointerDown, from Space/Enter, from unpauseGame and from toggleMute; it handles the WebKit-only "interrupted" state and plays a one-sample buffer to actually unlock iOS. Mute must never stop musicTick — the groove, the score from it and the visual beat all ride the same clock.

name: beep, panAt and PENT
summary: The thirty-call-site sound-effect voice, the screen-x panner, and the fourteen-degree pentatonic every effect speaks in.
detail: Owns beep (2920-2965), panAt (2966) and PENT/PENT_BASE (2981-2983). PENT is rescaled per level by applyLevelMusic, so every effect transposes with the key; degrees 0-4 are the band's and 4-13 are the player's. beep applies the black hole's gravitational redshift (2934-2940) on a squared curve reaching a perfect fourth at exit, and only during phase 2.

name: LV, the six-level table
summary: Six rows of dl0 / end / name / key / card lines — the finish lines, the transposition ladder and the intro cards.
detail: Owns LV (3042-3113) and the long curriculum argument above it. dl0 is the level floor read by dl(); end is the finish line read by update; key scales PENT; mech rows are drawn on the level card and are checked against MECHANICS.md. LEVEL_MAX is derived at 3115. Level 6 ends at Infinity because it is the authored frontier, not an endless-mode rule.

name: MODES, REC and the record keys
summary: One difficulty row (skill, every knob the identity element) plus the mode-suffixed localStorage record keys.
detail: Owns LEVEL_MAX (3115), MODE/MODES (3150-3155), MD (3156), REC (3171), recKey (3172) and useMode (3173). Every pressure expression multiplies by an MD() knob, so a second mode is a derivative and never a second implementation; check.mjs fails the build if a knob stops being neutral or is declared without a call site. The unsuffixed cometloop: keys are skill's and always were, so retiring chill migrated nothing.

name: the powerup lab
summary: A sandbox flag, not a mode: ten pickable orbs on a board whose difficulty clock is pinned at LAB_DL and which writes nothing to the device.
detail: Owns LAB_ORBS (3207-3225), LAB_DL (3227), LAB (3228) and labGhost (3234). LAB.on gates the record writes in die, the lesson writes in firstMeet and hop, the run counter in startGame, and every telemetry event except powerup_lab_started. enterMenu is the only clear of LAB.on. It must never become a MODES row — a pinned clock is not a difficulty.

name: the pause flag and its count-in
summary: Pause is a flag that stops the clock, not a game state: update returns before G.t+=dt, which freezes every deadline in the file at once.
detail: Owns PAUSE_COUNT/PAUSE_COOL (3272-3273), PAUSE (3274), pauseNow, pausedSeconds, frozen (3295), canPause, pauseAudio, pauseGame and unpauseGame. frozen() is read by update (7736) and by both input handlers so they can never disagree. Paused duration is measured on performance.now, never on the clamped frame delta. The board is hidden while paused and re-arming is on a cooldown, or the escape hatch becomes a difficulty change.

name: PROG, PROGB and the per-level parts
summary: Six verse progressions, six choruses with their rotation offsets, and the per-level arp, riff, solo and seventh tables.
detail: Owns PROG (3354), ARPL (3405), RIFFL (3409), SOLOL (3416), PROGB (3483), CHOFF (3507), CHOR_HOLD (3516), SEVB (3523), ARPBL (3533), applySect (3539) and applyLevelMusic (3547). applySect is the ONLY writer of CH and ARP; it copies a row set and everything downstream follows. Every chord must stay diatonic to its level's natural minor — the SFX pentatonic is scaled into the same mode and one borrowed chord puts the whole effects layer out of tune.

name: braam, soundImpact and the three cues
summary: The signature whaa, the three-kind impact voice, and the closed cue vocabulary: unlock, lesson, state-open/close.
detail: Owns braam (3556), soundImpact (3566, which only answers nova, hyper and orbit), cueUnlock (3602), cueLesson (3610) and cueState (3617). Each cue means exactly one thing and is never borrowed: cueUnlock is tier banners only, cueLesson is first-encounter lessons only, cueState is a standing bonus opening or closing. All three route through cueTone so they land on the grid.

name: levelComplete
summary: Ends a level: flushes the interrupted lesson, rolls the upgrade offer, carries the run totals forward and fires the cleared-level event.
detail: Owns levelComplete. Called from update at the finish line when there is no audio (7938) and from the star dive's exit (8123). It sets state to lvend and fills G.carry* — score, orbits, lands, streak, groove and accumulated time — which startGame reads back. The level record itself moves in die(), not here, so the announcement fires exactly once.

name: readLocal, loadPrefs and savePref
summary: localStorage is the real store, under the historical cometloop: prefix, with an optional async window.storage folded in by Math.max.
detail: Owns readLocal (3676), loadPrefs (3679-3754) and savePref (3755). loadPrefs runs once at 5104, immediately after G is declared and after the cloud session has been restored, so the first window.storage read is a real one. cometloop:level and cometloop:mode are deliberately never read — both hold retired meanings. Every write is wrapped: private-mode Safari throws.

name: the optional account and record sync
summary: Installs a window.storage backed by /api/progress while signed in, so records sync through a seam loadPrefs already had.
detail: Owns CLOUD_ORIGIN (3785), CLOUD, cloudTok, cloudApi/cloudAuthed, cloudPull/cloudPush/cloudPushNow, cloudAdopt, savePrefLocal, cloudInstallStorage/cloudRemoveStorage, the session helpers and cloudSubmit. The merge is done server-side by max, so a device can post without reading first and can never lower a record. Nothing here may ever sit between a tap and a comet moving; every failure is silent.

name: the DOM account panel
summary: The only part of the runtime that touches real DOM nodes — four views behind one door, guarded so a stubbed document cannot throw.
detail: Owns acEl/acH/acSub/acBody (4028), acOn, AC_DOM (4043), esc (4050), num, openAccount/closeAccount, acRender (4080-4204) and the action helpers. AC_DOM is the feature gate: every harness but one runs this file against a stubbed DOM. esc() is the only thing between a stranger's twelve-character display name and script execution on another player's device. The panel exists only on the title screen and keyDown returns early while it is open.

name: track()
summary: Anonymous PostHog events POSTed with sendBeacon and no SDK, suppressed entirely for lab runs.
detail: Owns POSTHOG_KEY/HOST (4282-4283), TELE_OK (4284), TELE_ID (4289) and track (4299-4343). track stamps swipe_mode, play_mode and the optional account_id on every event and forces $process_person_profile:false. TELE_OK is false on file: and localhost so dev and tests send nothing. The lab is silenced at this one choke point rather than by tagging, so a later event inherits the suppression for free.

name: swipeOut, swipeLean and swipeWords
summary: The single expression of the two swipe mental models — radial (out from the hub) and screen (up is out) — plus the sentence that describes whichever is chosen.
detail: Owns GEST (4348), SWIPE_MODE (4364), swipeWords (4372), swipeOut (4376) and swipeLean (4385). Both gesture resolution paths — the mid-drag commit in pointerMove and the lift decision in pdEnd — call swipeOut, so the two can never drift apart. The radial normal uses (cos a, AY sin a) because the arena is an ellipse. Every player-facing sentence about the hop must come from swipeWords.

name: say, sayNow and annPump
summary: One announcement queue with priority and a shelf life, so six systems cannot overwrite each other's single line.
detail: Owns CW/WARN/FADE/HOP (4392-4393), ANN (4403), annNext, say (4405), sayNow (4409) and annPump (4410). annPump runs once per frame from update (7783); it yields to a banner younger than 2.6s, drops expired lines rather than shouting them late, and spaces lines 2.8s apart. There is no full-screen flash channel any more — the comment at 4424 says so and flashHit was deleted.

name: dl() and the pressure curves
summary: One clock in difficulty-seconds, and six curves keyed off it: speed, warning, shard cap, arrival gap, ember cap and ember gap.
detail: Owns age (4425), dl (4435), dlOld (4451, dead), SPEED_MAX/speedAt (4459-4460), warnTime (4483), shardCap (4504), spawnGap (4539), rookie (4572), firstShardAt (4586), emberCap and emberGap (4590-4591). dl returns the level floor LV[level-1].dl0 plus a re-run of the gentle opening ramp, scaled by MD().clock; the lab pins it at LAB_DL and the intro returns 0. Moving dl moves all six curves together in the proportions they were tuned in — that is the whole point.

name: TIERS, tierIndex and the derived rungs
summary: Thirteen rungs of the unlock ladder with their dl thresholds, banner names and lesson sentences, plus the hop-gate that holds the exam until the first hop.
detail: Owns TIERS (4652-4739), T_VOICE (4749), T_SKY (4757), SHAPE_RANK (4768), tierIndex (4770) and featuredTier (4814). T_VOICE and T_SKY are derived by name lookup, not by ordinal, so inserting a rung cannot silently re-time the audio ladder. tierIndex holds at SECOND RING until the first landed hop, with a thirty-difficulty-second release valve, and is disabled in the lab where the clock is frozen. Every tier sub is word-for-word its MEET lesson.

name: pickType and shieldMax
summary: Chooses the next formation: an unmet shape insists until its lesson lands, otherwise a rank-weighted pool that only starts weighting past dl 340.
detail: Owns pickType (4818-4927) and shieldMax (4928). Called once per spawnSpike. Exclusions are duplicated across the insist loop and the pool loop by convention — a precondition added to one and not the other lets the insist path spawn what the pool refuses. Two live twin pairs is the ceiling past dl 340; a gate and a saucer may never share a board.

name: UPG and rollOffer
summary: Twelve upgrade tiles with their own icon painters, drawn three at a time on the level card without replacement.
detail: Owns UPG (4937-5001), starPath (5002), upgOn (5006) and rollOffer (5008-5025). rollOffer is called only from levelComplete and only when a further level exists. Taken upgrades never repeat; declined ones may, once the fresh pool runs thin. Tiles gate on minLevel so a tile can only offer an upgrade to something the player has met. upgOn is read by nine effect sites.

name: G
summary: The single mutable game-state object: clocks, run counters, ring position, timed reward states, entity arrays and every draw envelope.
detail: Owns REV_FX (5027), SND_SEEN (5028) and G (5029-5103), followed immediately by loadPrefs() at 5104. G.t is real seconds and every deadline in the file is written against it; G.vt is the same clock scaled by G.tsCur and is what the visible world runs on. startGame resets it in two tiers — per-run fields guarded by `carried`, per-level fields unconditionally. G.beat is now written nowhere and read nowhere; it is dead state.

name: curR, posPlayer, effRing and the hit tests
summary: The comet's eased radius during a hop, the ring collision runs on, magnet star flight, and the swept-arc hit test.
detail: Owns curR (5106), posPlayer (5119), effRing (5120), MAGNET_* (5125), starfallFlightPos (5126), starVisualPos (5133), updateMagnetStar (5136), starTouchesPlayer (5155) and sweptHit (5166). effRing switches at hopP 0.5 so collision is on ring indices while curR eases with an overshoot clamped to 6u. sweptHit covers the whole angle travelled this frame, which is what stops tunnelling after a dropped frame.

name: burst, ripple, arcFlash and popup
summary: The four particle/marker spawners every celebration in the game is assembled from, with the popup cloud capped at four.
detail: Owns burst (5175), ripple (5181), arcFlash (5185) and popup (5186-5197). arcFlash follows the ring it happened on rather than stamping a circle across the arena. popup shifts the oldest out at four, and the draw dims survivors by age so the newest is the news. All four are drawn in draw() inside the camera dolly.

name: novaBlast and novaConvert
summary: An expanding front that converts shards on contact, landing each ember on the player's own ring as a spaced necklace and playing an ascending sixteenth run.
detail: Owns NOVA_SP (5214), NOVA_RUN (5215), novaBlast (5222), novaConvert (5236) and ignite (5287). The front is advanced in update (7825-7838) against a captured target list, so it cannot eat shards that arrived after the blast. Each blast carries whichever speed is faster: the tuned 560u/s or the one that clears the ring system in 0.62s on a large viewport. novaConvert is also the hypernova plough and the slipstream clear.

name: checkMile
summary: Fires a centre ripple and a two-note cue every 250 points, in the level's own key.
detail: Owns checkMile. Called from the ember pickup and from the orbit payout. The step is 250 rather than 50 because at mid-game rates the smaller step was a celebration metronome. Its pitches are ratios over CH[0][0] so level 1 is bit-identical to the old absolute literals.

name: hitTol, sep, behindPad and farFromAll
summary: The placement guarantee: clearance expressed as a multiple of a shard's own hit width, asymmetric around the comet's heading.
detail: Owns hitTol (5316), sep (5317), BEHIND_MIN (5356), behindPad (5357) and farFromAll (5361). Clearance is a multiple of hitTol so it is correct on every ring and every screen size. The exclusion follows travel, not position: full clearance ahead, a short time-based pad behind, which is what closed the camping sanctuary. While any live gate segment is on the board behindPad returns 0 and the bubble goes symmetric again.

name: spawnStar, mkSpike, the saucer constants and reverseEscape
summary: Places an ember, builds a shard with its warn stretched to the beat grid, and proves a reversal has somewhere to open onto.
detail: Owns spawnStar (5374), mkSpike (5380), GATE_ESCAPE (5401), SAUCER_LAG/CHG/BEAM/HOP (5422-5425), SAUCER_COOL (5434), saucerOK (5435) and reverseEscape (5440). mkSpike stretches s.warn by up to one eighth so a shard turns lethal on a beat subdivision. reverseEscape is checked at spawn time for gates, which is why gates are exempt from the behind-pad rule.

name: MEET and firstMeet
summary: The first-encounter lesson table and the eleven guards that decide whether a lesson fires now, defers, or is spent.
detail: Owns MEET (5472-5593) and firstMeet (5594-5668). A lesson defers — without setting the seen bit — during the lab, inside 9s of the last one, during a hop rehearsal, under a fresh banner, inside a black hole, while a timed reward is running, or with an armed shard near the player. Soft lessons additionally wait until the red lesson has landed on this device. Each MEET sentence is word-for-word the tier banner sub and the death coach line; changing one means changing all three.

name: spawnSpike
summary: Places the chosen formation with eighteen relaxing attempts, downgrading to a single rather than shipping an unanswerable trap.
detail: Owns spawnSpike. Called from update (8412) when the spike timer expires, the board is under shardCap, no lesson is up and the first-shard delay has passed. The saucer skips the placement loop entirely — its position is a function of the player's. firstMeet is called at each SUCCESS site, never before the loop, or a dense board spends the once-ever lesson on a formation that never existed.

name: the timed reward states
summary: Mirror, scorch's sector burn, slipstream, the star route, and the per-frame motion of stars, orbs and the mirror comet.
detail: Owns MIRROR_BEATS (5880), SCORCH_SECS/BURN_SECT/BURN_LIFE (5891), SLIP_* (5892), STAR_ROUTE_* (5893), burnIdx (5894), burning (5895), layStarTrail (5901) and updateOrbMotion (5913-5966). updateOrbMotion is called once per frame from update (8257) and is where tickStarfall runs. The burn is stored per ring as a fixed sector array so arcs cannot overlap or leak.

name: spawnPow and the guarantee ladder
summary: The ordered orb placement: three intro orbs, then one guaranteed introduction per level, then a level-gated weighted roll.
detail: Owns POW_INTRO (5967), POW_LESSON (5968-5969) and spawnPow (5970-6121). The two black-hole branches sit directly below POW_INTRO because the branches they jump are patient (their flags persist) while a per-placement die that is never rolled is simply gone. POWPOOL (6080-6082) is filtered by the same level floors as the guarantees and renormalised, so removing or adding an orb never changes the survivors' ratios to each other.

name: startGame
summary: Starts a run OR advances a level from the same 228 lines, with `carried` as the one signal that distinguishes them.
detail: Owns startGame. Called from beginIntro, startLab, startFromSelect, retry and both level-card commit paths. Fields guarded by `carried` are per-RUN (the intro trio, the guarantee flags, didHop/didLap/didReverse, the sky journey, saidChor); everything else is re-baselined per LEVEL, which is the same scale telemetry's `seconds` uses. It re-arms each orb guarantee only for levels still ahead of the level the run opens on.

name: die()
summary: Ends the run: records, coaching, the killer lesson re-arm, the struggle streak, the death sound on the next eighth, and run_ended.
detail: Owns die. Called from updateSpikes when a lethal contact finds no shield, and from endBlackHole on a failed escape. It skips a live black hole straight to the closing warp so the mode cannot complete post-mortem. The best-score and deepest-level writes are both guarded by !LAB.on and, for the level record, by G.startLevel===1. run_ended carries the whole run-shape payload the balance questions are answered from.

name: reverse, reverseFX and retry
summary: The primary verb: flips direction instantly, banks the travelled arc toward the sky journey, and defers its sound so a swipe can roll it back.
detail: Owns reverseFX (6576), reverse (6600), commitReverseFX (6631) and retry (6640). reverse(true) from a pointer flips direction but schedules the effects REV_FX later; pointerMove rolls the whole thing back — lap, streak, didReverse and lapCut — if the gesture becomes a swipe. The scoring lap resets, but the distance travelled is banked into G.skyW, which is what stopped tapping players from never seeing a new world.

name: the menu, pickers and first flight
summary: Every non-playing state entered through its own function, each of which resets the arena behind it.
detail: Owns enterSwipeSel, enterMenu (the ONLY clear of LAB.on), enterPowerSel, startLab, enterLevelSel, menuStep, pickOrb, toggleGhost, beginIntro, introPrompt/Feedback/Action, finishIntro, introTick, enterRunStart, leaveMenu, openLab and startFromSelect. enterPowerSel resets the black hole and every timed reward outright, because bhTick keeps running across a death and would otherwise tick on the picker. Each picker is a decision: its background starts nothing.

name: cardDone, flushLesson and bump
summary: Records a shown level card, closes out a lesson (including one cut short by a death), and acknowledges a swipe with nowhere to go.
detail: Owns cardDone (6901), flushLesson (6911) and bump (6922). flushLesson clears every spotlit specimen and fires lesson_shown with a `cut` flag; without the cut flush the exact lessons interrupted by the death they should explain vanished from the funnel. bump is deliberately not counted as a misread gesture.

name: hop(step)
summary: The second verb: changes ring, marks the wake, clears red under slipstream, and plays the arriving ring rather than the one left.
detail: Owns hop. Called from pointerMove's mid-drag commit, pdEnd's lift decision, the arrow keys and menuDemo. A hop with nowhere to go bumps and still plays a performer note — the one input you can play purely for the music. The everHopped write is guarded by !LAB.on so a sandbox swipe cannot spend the once-ever hop rehearsal.

name: runTime, tierLabel, levelName, runSummary and doShare
summary: The plain-text artifact a player shares, and the two ladders it is careful to keep apart.
detail: Owns runTime (7017), tierLabel (7021), levelName (7038), PIPDT (7062), runSummary (7063) and doShare (7089). Everything the player reads is G.level; tierLabel survives only for telemetry. runSummary names a picked start level explicitly so the share text cannot claim an unqualified level 6. doShare prefers navigator.share and falls back to the clipboard.

name: the on-screen control rectangles
summary: Every tappable region during play, defined once so the input handler and the draw pass cannot disagree.
detail: Owns muteRect (7106), pauseRect (7114), inPause (7115), shieldRect (7122), inMute (7126), deadSeqDone (7133), shareRect (7139) and inShare (7151). The arena answers a tap anywhere, so every one of these must be tested BEFORE the reversal in pointerDown or it can never be pressed. shareRect is clamped off TAP TO RETRY and inShare refuses in the lab.

name: pointerDown, pointerMove and pdEnd
summary: One gesture at a time: a tap reverses instantly and speculatively, and the same pointer becoming a swipe rolls the reversal back.
detail: Owns pd (7161), pointerDown (7162), RADIAL_MIN (7291), pointerMove (7292), pdEnd (7328), pointerUp and pointerCancel. Order in pointerDown is the contract: frozen panel, pause, mute, share, intro skip, then the state pickers, then the lab door, then the death screen, then the arena. A swipe commits mid-drag once its radial lean passes RADIAL_MIN of the travel, otherwise at lift with a looser threshold.

name: keyDown and the DOM listener block
summary: The desktop control scheme, guarded against auto-repeat and disabled while the account panel or the pause panel owns the screen.
detail: Owns keyDown (7411-7494) and the listener installation at 7495-7502, which only runs when there is no external loop. e.repeat is rejected outright — a held Space used to call reverse twenty times a second and pin the comet inside 0.23 rad. Mute stays live while frozen; Space or Enter presses RESUME rather than starting a second pause.

name: the trail, the menu demo and the blink cycle
summary: The comet ribbon sampler, the twelve-second scripted title-screen demo, and the on-grid shutter phase.
detail: Owns trailCap (7512), pushTrail (7513), DEMO (7525), menuDemo (7526), BLINK (7542), blinkPhase (7545), BDUTY (7553), duty (7554) and armed (7555). BLINK is two beats, so a shutter flickers on the musical grid; a pair runs at duty 0.5 so exactly one side is lethal at every instant, which is what makes its lesson literally true.

name: updateSpikes
summary: Advances every shard, runs the saucer state machine, and is the ONE lethal-contact site in the game.
detail: Owns updateSpikes. Called with lethal=true from update (8760), with lethal=false from menuDemo and from the death-screen branch. Phase 0 is the telegraph, 1 lethal, 2 fading. The lethal branch is ordered hypernova plough, then shield, then die; labGhost() short-circuits the whole thing so nothing downstream fires. The near-miss DODGED branch never counts a body that was never going to touch you.

name: update(dt)
summary: The whole simulation frame: the freeze gate, every envelope decay, the tier ratchet, spawning, pickups and collision.
detail: Owns update. Called from runtimeStep with a delta clamped to 0.05s. The single `return` inside frozen() at 7737 is the entire pause mechanism — G.t+=dt sits below it, so every deadline in the file freezes together. Order matters: clocks and envelopes, bhTick and bedTick, the time-scale ease, particles, the state early-returns for menu/pickers/dead, the finale, the tier ratchet, motion, spawn timers, pickups, then updateSpikes last.

name: the faceted artifact sprite bank
summary: Bakes every gameplay object as a faceted, key-lit sprite keyed on u and DPR, preferring a host texture when the manifest supplies one.
detail: Owns artifactBank (8761), artifactMaterials (8762-8774), the drawing helpers, artifactSprite (8868), artifactStar (8929), artifactPower (8940), artifactShard (8947), drawShardOutline (8973, dead), rimLight (8993) and drawPow (9005). artifactSprite reads host.getTexture — the raw parameter, not runtimeHost — so a host explicitly passed as null would throw here where the rest of the file is safe. The bank is invalidated whenever u or DPR changes and is cleared by runtimeDestroy.

name: text, fitSz and textFx
summary: The single font stack and the three text primitives every screen in the game draws through.
detail: Owns F (9047), text (9049), fitSz (9060) and textFx (9072). fitSz shrinks a string until it fits a width, which is what lets the lesson sentences grow without a layout pass. textFx is the gradient-and-glow variant used for headlines. Nothing else may call ctx.fillText directly if it wants the house font.

name: drawBloom and the halo chain
summary: Redraws every light into a quarter-resolution buffer, builds its halo on the GPU when the FX chain is up and on two extra discs when it is not, then composites additively.
detail: Owns BLOOM_DIV/BLOOM_ALPHA (9116), the HALO_* dials (9134-9137), the buffers, bloomHalo (9146), bloomDot (9147) and drawBloom (9156-9286). bloomHalo is set from !FX.on once per frame, before the dot loop, so a mid-frame GL failure can never leave half the lights haloed. The composite resets to the base transform because the bright pass draws without the camera dolly.

name: drawRingGlow (unreferenced)
summary: A four-layer lit arc under the comet tinted by its ring — defined, tuned, and called from nowhere in the current build.
detail: Owns RING_LIT (9287) and drawRingGlow (9288-9314). There is no call site: draw() states at 10745 that "Ring light is supplied by the single path pass above". The constant is still listed as a tunable, so an agent asked to adjust the lit track will otherwise edit a table nothing reads.

name: tailRibbon and drawTail
summary: The comet ribbon as one tapered polygon, doubled by a lagging violet ghost while time is dilated.
detail: Owns tailRibbon (9315) and drawTail (9382). The ghost is the same ribbon minus its most recent samples and is drawn first, so the live cyan lies on top of its own past; the whole pass is behind the same G.tsCur test the slow-mo vignette uses and never runs under reduced motion. Width and colour ride the groove and the hypernova envelope.

name: beatPhase, drawBeat and musPos
summary: A ring that contracts onto the comet over the half-beat BEFORE each beat and lands, plus the audible bar position the sky and HUD read.
detail: Owns beatPhase (9413), drawBeat (9421) and musPos (9445). beatPhase derives the quarter boundary from MU.next and MU.step parity — the same derivation judgeTiming's quarter anchor uses, so the thing taught and the thing judged are one thing. musPos free-runs on wall time when there is no audio clock, deliberately, so a muted player still sees a world that breathes in time.

name: the background fragment shader and its context
summary: One full-screen triangle whose fragment shader paints the whole world — globe, rings, atmosphere, dust, stars and the black-hole lensing.
detail: Owns GL_SCALE/GL_MOTION (9457-9458), GL (9459), GL_FS (9460-9673), glInit (9674), glResize (9709) and the inert glRipple/glShear hooks (9720-9721). glInit is called once at 10020 against runtimeHost.background or #bg; a failure is permanent for the frame and hands the backdrop to drawCalmSky. GL_MOTION is now 1.0 — CLAUDE.md still records 0.25.

name: SKY, skyMix and the scene accent
summary: Interpolates the eight worlds into one uniform set and holds at most one authored event envelope at a time.
detail: Owns SKY (9722), lerp3, skyMaterialHue (9724), skyMix (9729), SCENE_RANK/SCENE_TINT (9745-9750), scenePulse (9751), sceneAccent (9759), skyWake (9773) and skyStep (9777). scenePulse refuses a duplicate or a lower-ranked event while one is live, so audio and gameplay reporting the same earned moment cannot double-pulse. skyMix crossfades only over the last 20% of a world, so travel reads as arrival rather than as a constant dissolve.

name: drawCalmSky, the no-WebGL path
summary: A CPU sky sharing the globe, ring and cloud parameters with the shader: a half-resolution material cache plus native-resolution stars.
detail: Owns SKY_2D (9787), skyHash/skyNoise/skyCloud/skyCalm (9788-9812) and drawCalmSky (9813-9928). Called only from draw (10694) when GL.on is false. The material cache is keyed on size, world, arena radii and the scenic clock, so it rebuilds on a schedule rather than per frame. It must stay self-contained: no external artwork is required for it to render.

name: glRender and the sky material binding
summary: Uploads the interpolated world, the arena geometry, the live flow envelopes and up to three host textures, then draws one triangle.
detail: Owns skyAdvanceClock (9929), skyCharge (9936), SKY_MATERIALS (9941), skyTexture (9942), glBindSkyMaterials (9947), glRender (9969), the boot call at 10020 and the context-loss listeners at 10021-10083. skyCharge feeds the starfall build back into the sky. Texture lookups go through runtimeHost.getTexture and fall back to a 1x1 blank with uArt flags, so a missing manifest entry is a degraded sky rather than a broken one.

name: the second WebGL context: gaussian halo and chromatic composite
summary: An offscreen GL context that blurs the bright buffer at two levels and composites them with a slight chromatic spread.
detail: Owns FX_A (10084), FX_MIDW/FX_WIDEW/FX_SPREAD/FX_AB (10085-10097), FX (10098), the shaders, fxInit (10196), fxTarget, fxResize, fxBlur, fxRender (10302) and the boot and context-loss handling at 10347-10379. fxRender must detect a lost context explicitly — a lost GL context does not throw, it goes quiet, and a quiet failure would composite an empty canvas. Its failure is permanent for the session and the disc fallback takes over.

name: the rails, the power atmosphere and the impact log
summary: Draws the orbit rails as lit metal, the standing-reward atmosphere, and records the last seven earned impacts for their own pass.
detail: Owns impactColor (10380), impactHalo (10386), impactRecord (10397), drawOrbitalRails (10405) and drawPowerAtmosphere (10433). impactRecord is called from scenePulse (9756), so one earned event feeds both the sky envelope and the arena decoration. The impact list is filtered by run start, so a prior run can never light a new one.

name: the dust wake and G.currentFlow
summary: Thirty-six persistent world-space dust strands that keep the direction of committed gestures, and the envelope object the audio and the sky both read.
detail: Owns currentWakeReset (10463), currentWakeTurn (10476), currentWakeHop (10489), currentWakeUpdate (10494) and drawCurrentWake (10556). Reset runs from startGame (6227); turn from reverseFX (6577); hop from hop (6966); update from update (7917 and 8257) on the dilated delta. G.currentFlow.turn/hop/radial/dir/magnet/scorch/release/bh/travel is read by orbitMusicState, performerHit's panner and glRender's uniforms — it is the one shared motion vocabulary in the build.

name: drawImpactEvents, drawSingularity and drawCometFins
summary: The earned-impact contours, the black hole's shadow and lensing, and the comet's heading fins.
detail: Owns drawImpactEvents (10582), drawSingularity (10608) and drawCometFins (10655). drawSingularity is drawn before the camera dolly is applied (10698) because the hole is anchored to the arena centre, and the hub lamp is separately suppressed inside it — two independent passes both had to be told.

name: draw()
summary: The world render pass in a fixed order: sky, singularity, dolly, wake, rails, burn, stars, orbs, shards, novas, laps, tail, comet, particles, bloom, popups.
detail: Owns draw. Called from runtimeRender inside a save/restore that also repairs the incoming Phaser transform. It resets the transform and the two most-leaked context attributes at the top because a thrown frame otherwise poisons every later one. paX/paY are set here (10696) and read by posAt everywhere else. There is no full-screen flash or impact frame any more — the comment at 11273 is explicit.

name: the five drawn controls
summary: The shield readout, the share pill, the pause icon, the pause blackout panel and the mute icon.
detail: Owns drawShieldBtn (11277), drawShareBtn (11310), drawPauseBtn (11332), drawPausePanel (11348) and drawMute (11387). All five are called at the very end of draw, after drawHUD, so the pause blackout covers the score and the shard count as well as the arena. The shield strip is a readout, not a button — its frame was removed so it stops inviting a press it no longer answers.

name: the glyphs, hint ladder and message card
summary: The teaching glyph set, the retiring hint ladder, the centre message card, the run HUD and the front-screen panel primitives.
detail: Owns hintGlyph (11423), hintText (11513), drawLadder (11550, unreferenced), runMessage (11571), hudLines (11600), drawMessageCard (11611), drawPowerStatus (11643), drawRunHUD (11671), drawFinalePath (11719) and the frontPath/frontPanel/frontLaunch/frontLogo/frontHeading primitives (11798-11887). hintText retires each line on the learned action rather than restarting it every run. runMessage guarantees one message owns the quiet centre.

name: drawHUD
summary: The lesson veil plus a six-way dispatch on G.state: run HUD, level card, swipe chooser, title, level picker, lab picker, death screen.
detail: Owns drawHUD. Called from draw (11265). It publishes the hit rectangles the input handler reads back — G.menuRects, G.lvSelRects, G.powSelRects, G.offerRects, G.labRect, G.swipeRect, G.introSkipRect — so layout and hit testing are one definition. The final else is the death screen; there is no separate paused state, which is exactly why pause had to be a flag.

name: the returned runtime surface
summary: runtimeStep, runtimeRender, frame, pause, resume, back, snapshot, disposeGpu and destroy — everything the Phaser scene drives.
detail: Owns last (12212), runtimeStep (12213), runtimeRender (12219), frame (12239), runtimePause (12245), runtimeResume (12255), runtimeBack (12261), runtimeSnapshot (12270), runtimeDisposeGpu (12281), runtimeDestroy (12304), the no-host boot at 12324 and the returned object at 12329. runtimeRender saves and restores Phaser's incoming transform and keeps the first draw error on window.__drawErr. runtimeDestroy must release listeners, the audio context, both GL contexts and every sprite cache.

name: what is baked, declared or written and never read
summary: Eleven of sixteen baked sprites, five whole functions, six tables and G.beat exist in the shipped file with no reader.
detail: Silently dead: makeCanvas, buildStarField/starField, bgStars, nebulas, MOTES, RING_MULT, BUILD_SRC, DROP_STEP/DROP_STEP_MAX, LAND_WIN/LAND_PERFECT, schedulePreDrop, dlOld, drawShardOutline, drawRingGlow, drawLadder, and SPR.shard/shardDrift/shardBlink/shieldRing/powShield/powWarpO/powWarpI/powNova/powHyper/mote/pip/shock. G.beat is reset and decayed but never set or read. Declared-inert and load-bearing as documentation: tryLand, LOOP, LOOPQ, PLAY.tape, glRipple, glShear.

name: buildBus()
summary: Builds the WebAudio graph once and assigns A; idempotent, and calls buildBed at the end.
detail: Signature buildBus(). Returns early if A already exists or AC is null. Node names that matter downstream: A.world (SFX), A.bed (music), A.hole (the drop silence), A.pump (sidechain), A.band, A.perf (the player, bypassing hole and bedDuck), A.dly (dotted-eighth dub delay), A.send (reverb).

name: buildBed()
summary: Starts the four continuously-running detuned pad voices, generates the shared noise buffer, and initialises MU.
detail: Signature buildBed(). Called only from the last line of buildBus. The pad is eight oscillators (four voices x two detuned unisons) retuned by setTargetAtTime, never restarted. NOISE is 1.5 s so the drop riser's 1.73 s sweep does not loop audibly.

name: note(f,t,dur,type,g,cut,pan,bus,echo)
summary: The one-shot musical voice: oscillator into a closing lowpass, optional pan, optional dub send, routed to A.bed unless a bus is named.
detail: Nine positional arguments; only the first five are ever required. Passing A.perf as `bus` is what puts a sound on the player's own path — drier (0.28 send instead of 0.5) and outside the drop's hole. Roughly a hundred call sites. Silent when muted or before the bus exists.

name: subF(f)
summary: Octave-doubles any frequency below 40 Hz so a low level key keeps its pitch class and still moves air on a phone.
detail: Signature subF(f) -> number. Guards every dedicated sub voice: the drop boom, the payoff floor, the braam and the layer-three drone. Without it level 6's roots fall to 23-31 Hz, which reproduces on nothing the game ships to.

name: beep(f,d,type,g,slide,when,pan,wet)
summary: The sound-effect voice, kept at its original signature because thirty call sites depend on it; applies the black hole redshift.
detail: Routes to A.world, so it is audible through the band duck. `when` schedules on the audio clock rather than setTimeout. Inside black-hole phase 2 it multiplies f and slide by a squared curve reaching 2^(-5/12); phases 1 and 3 keep their pitch so the entry and exit cues stay recognisable.

name: soundImpact(kind,strength)
summary: The three-voice impact for exactly three kinds — nova, hyper and orbit — and a silent no-op for anything else.
detail: Returns immediately unless kind is nova, hyper or orbit. Ducks the bed, then plays a sub, a body and (for nova/hyper) a filtered noise sweep through A.world. Called from the hypernova pickup, the nova pickup and the milestone orbit payout.

name: cueTone(fn)
summary: Hands a callback the delay that lands its notes on the next free sixteenth, so the game's replies form a note run instead of a cloud.
detail: Signature cueTone(fn) where fn receives a delay in seconds relative to AC.currentTime. Falls through to fn(0) when there is no scheduler. A slot already taken cascades one sixteenth, capped a beat out. Twenty-four call sites: embers, orbits, shields, hops, milestones, lessons, the finale.

name: gridNear()
summary: Returns the nearest sixteenth grid point, which may sit slightly in the past — the caller clamps.
detail: Returns AC.currentTime+0.015 when there is no schedule. Deliberately not clamped internally: a clamped now+12ms would make every front-half tap a unique timestamp and defeat performerHit's one-note-per-slot dedupe.

name: judgeTiming(x,y)
summary: Scores a tap on three tiers against a learned device bias and returns the resulting ON BEAT chain value.
detail: Returns G.groove (0-8). Only performerHit calls it. The quarter anchor is MU.next plus half a beat when MU.step is odd; anchoring it wrong judges the offbeat, which musiccheck catches. The steadyhand upgrade widens the window from 0.032 to 0.045.

name: performerHit(kind,dir,ring)
summary: Plays the player's own instrument for a tap or a hop, on the grid, on A.perf, as a chord tone of the current bar.
detail: kind is "rev" or "hop"; ring is the ring being ARRIVED at. Returns nothing. Refuses while frozen, outside play, with no audio, or inside a black hole. It also drives PLAY.heat (+0.26 per input) which is the engagement term the whole arrangement opens on.

name: musicStep(i,t,k)
summary: Schedules one eighth of the arrangement at audio time t, with i the step index in the 32-step loop and k the normalised difficulty.
detail: The dispatch order is the contract: section seam (i===0 only), chord retune, black hole, payoff, armed fire, star dive, then the ordinary arrangement. Everything below a `return` in this function is silent for that eighth. k is min(1, dl()/150).

name: chTone(ix) and chI(bar)
summary: Resolves an index into the chord sounding right now — 0-3 walk the voicing, each block of four an octave up.
detail: chI applies the chorus rotation CHOFF so a chorus can open off-tonic while CH[0] stays the tonic chord twenty-five readers assume. Everything the player triggers speaks through chTone, which is why a tap is harmonically correct by construction rather than by luck.

name: applySect(s) and applyLevelMusic()
summary: The only writer of the live CH and ARP tables; applyLevelMusic additionally rescales PENT by the level key.
detail: applySect(0) is the verse, applySect(1) the chorus; it copies a row set from PROG/PROGB and ARPL/ARPBL. It touches tables, never oscillators — the pad retunes at the next bar line. applyLevelMusic is called from startGame and always opens on the verse.

name: musicTick()
summary: Walks MU.step forward until the schedule reaches 160 ms ahead of the audio clock, at most sixteen steps per call.
detail: Called only from bedTick. Detects a gap greater than 0.4 s and abandons the section rather than replaying it compressed. When not playing it ends any live section and zeroes MU.next.

name: bedTick(dt)
summary: The only writer of BED.g and of the pad voice weights, and the function that calls musicTick.
detail: Called unconditionally from update. Sets the pad level, the pad filter cutoff, A.band, the four voice weights from orbit pressure, drains BEATQ and DROPQ, decays PLAY.heat, and enforces MU.payEnd as the section deadline. Nothing else may write BED.g.

name: duckBed(amount,rel)
summary: Dips A.bed and writes its own recovery in the same call; refuses to fire inside the drop hush.
detail: Six call sites: black-hole entry, the drum break, the milestone orbit, soundImpact, levelComplete and die. The hush guard at 2846 is currently unreachable because schedulePreDrop has no caller.

name: armDrop(why,src)
summary: Arms the next Starfall, or banks it into MU.pend when the music is busy, and plays the earn stab either way.
detail: Called from build (1324), from bedTick when a banked earning can finally fire (2751), and re-banked by endSection and startBlackHole. An earning is never discarded — the cooldown only stops two sections overlapping.

name: schedulePreDrop(tD)
summary: Writes the pre-drop hush automation on A.hole and BED.lp — and has no call site in the shipped file.
detail: Zero callers. Because of that MU.hushEnd and MU.lpLock are only ever 0, duckBed's hush guard never trips, and A.hole is written only by endSection's restore. The 34-line comment above it states the file's central audio rule (every duck writes its own undo) using a function that never runs.

name: fireDrop(t)
summary: Lands the payoff: sets MU.pay, the cooldown, the crown ring and the flavour, plays the impact stack, and queues the visual.
detail: Called from musicStep on an armed even eighth. Every pitch is an interval over CH[0][0] so the drop is in the level key. It deliberately schedules no kick at t — payoffStep's bar 0 fires one at the same instant. DROPQ.push(t) is what makes the picture wait for the sound.

name: payoffStep(t,ch,k)
summary: Plays one eighth of the eight-bar payoff section, including the sidechain pump and the per-level hook.
detail: n = PAY - MU.pay gives the position; pb is the bar, ps the eighth. Bars 2, 3 and 6 are the answering phrase (ANSWERL); bar 7 is the written descent. MU.crown raises the richness, MU.flavor colours the texture, MU.payN alternates the second ending.

name: endSection()
summary: Clears every interrupted musical phrase through one path, banks an unpaid earning, and restores A.hole and A.pump.
detail: Thirteen call sites. Banks only while the state is still playing — death and menu start clean. Always lands back on the verse. This is the belt-and-braces restore, not the mechanism: every duck is supposed to write its own undo.

name: toggleMute()
summary: Gates A.out, persists the choice, prints an acknowledgement, and ends any live section — but never stops the clock.
detail: Called from the mute rect, the M key and nothing else. Muting mid-section ends it rather than letting it run out against a silent bus. A silent run keeps the groove, the score from it, the drop and the visual beat.

name: orbitMusicState()
summary: Reduces the live orbit and the gesture wake to {active, q, turn, hop, radial, dir, pressure} for the pad and the chorus colour.
detail: Reads G.currentFlow, G.lapEmbers, G.lapAcc and G.lapStreak. Inactive during hypernova, overdrive, an armed or live payoff, a black hole, the finale, a starfall release and any freeze. Consumed by musicStep (1796) and bedTick (2733).

name: build(amount,src)
summary: The Starfall meter. Rejects every source but a completed star-fed orbit, then counts to dropNeed and arms.
detail: Signature build(amount, src). The guard at 1322 — src!=="orbit" || amount<0.04 — makes five of the six call sites no-ops: the per-second tick, the ember pickup, the hop, the tight tap and the near-miss all pass an amount or a source that is rejected. Only the 0.043 orbit call at 8404 survives.

name: startStarfall() and tickStarfall(dt)
summary: Opens the Starfall reward — a nova blast, three timed waves of guaranteed stars, and invulnerability for its whole length.
detail: startStarfall refuses outside play, during the intro, inside a black hole, or while one is already running. tickStarfall runs from updateOrbMotion and re-asserts G.invuln every frame so a black-hole detour cannot eat the earned safety. The result summary lands in G.starfallResult.

name: bhTick(dt)
summary: Advances the black hole through its four phases and is the only writer of RADII.
detail: Called from update whenever the state is playing OR the mode is active, so it can complete across a death. Phase 2 opens the fourth ring and pulls the comet inward every BH_PULL seconds; the closing phase withdraws every entity from the vanishing lane before its radius reaches zero.

name: frozen()
summary: The single predicate that says the world is not running — read by update and by both input handlers so they can never disagree.
detail: Returns PAUSE.on || PAUSE.resumeT>0, so it covers both the panel and the three-second count-in. canPause (3296) is its complement plus the cooldown.

name: dl()
summary: The difficulty clock in difficulty-seconds: the level floor plus a re-run of the gentle opening ramp, scaled by the mode.
detail: Returns 0 during the intro and LAB_DL in the lab. Everything that presses on the player keys off this one number, which is why the lab pins it and a future mode scales it rather than trimming six terms separately.

name: pickType()
summary: Chooses the next formation: the newest unmet shape insists until its lesson lands, otherwise a rank-weighted draw.
detail: Returns a formation type string. Both loops carry the same exclusions by duplication — twins capped at two pairs past dl 340, one wall at a time, no gate beside a saucer, dive and funnel need two rings. The rank weighting is identity below dl 340, so levels 1-3 are untouched by construction.

name: spawnSpike()
summary: Places one formation, trying eighteen times with relaxing clearance and downgrading rather than shipping a trap.
detail: Called from update on the spike timer. Gates and sliding gates downgrade to a single when reverseEscape fails; the saucer skips placement entirely. firstMeet is called only at a success site, and the unseen-type 1.6x telegraph is computed before the lesson stamps the seen bit.

name: farFromAll(a,ring,minP,minSpike,minStar,behind)
summary: The placement predicate: clear of the player along the heading, and clear of every spike, star and orb on that ring.
detail: With behind>0 the player term is asymmetric — full clearance ahead, only `behind` radians of pad behind; with behind falsy it is the old symmetric read, which is what stars, orbs and gate segments still use. Distances are radians and callers pass sep(ring,k) so the clearance is correct on every ring.

name: firstMeet(type)
summary: Shows a mechanic's once-per-device lesson, or defers it without spending it.
detail: Eleven guards, each of which returns WITHOUT setting G.seen so the next encounter re-offers. Sets G.teach (2.8 s), G.teachKind="see", G.teachType and G.teachHint, persists the seen set, and plays cueLesson. Never runs in the lab, and soft lessons wait for the red lesson to land first.

name: novaConvert(s,toRing)
summary: Turns one shard into embers on the player's ring, spaced along the lane, and plays the next degree of an ascending sixteenth run.
detail: Called by the nova front, the hypernova plough and the slipstream clear. The spacing walk steps 0.36 rad in the direction of travel until it finds room, so a converted wall reads as a necklace rather than a pile. RICH NOVA doubles the yield through the same walk.

name: sweptHit(target,tol)
summary: Tests whether the comet crossed an angle at any point during this frame, not just where it ended up.
detail: Uses G.sweep, G.prevAngle and G.dir. Every collision and pickup in the game goes through it, which is what stops tunnelling on a large screen or after a dropped frame.

name: effRing() and curR()
summary: The ring collision runs on during a hop (switching at the halfway point) and the eased radius the comet is drawn at.
detail: curR uses ease-out-back with a 6u clamp so the comet cannot visibly leave the track band; under reduced motion it falls back to smoothstep. Collision is on ring indices only — the two never disagree because effRing is the single source.

name: update(dt)
summary: The simulation frame. The one return inside frozen() is the entire pause mechanism.
detail: Called from runtimeStep with dt clamped to 0.05 s. G.t+=dt sits at 7752, below the freeze gate; sdt (8161) is the further-scaled delta the world moves on, and pdt (7815) is the presentation delta particles and the sky ride.

name: updateSpikes(sdt,lethal)
summary: Advances every shard and is the game's only lethal-contact site.
detail: lethal=false is used by the menu demo and the death screen so shards still animate without being able to kill. labGhost() short-circuits the whole lethal branch, so nothing downstream fires — no shield, no pip, no popup, no death.

name: startGame()
summary: Starts a run or advances a level; `carried` (a non-zero G.carryScore) is what distinguishes the two.
detail: Five call sites. Fields inside if(!carried) are per-run; everything else is per-level, which matches the scale telemetry's `seconds` uses. It silently pre-climbs G.tier and G.nRings for a level-2+ start so no banner fires over the card.

name: die()
summary: Ends the run, writes the records, arms the death coaching and the killer-lesson re-offer, and fires run_ended.
detail: Called from updateSpikes and from a failed black-hole escape. Every persisted write is guarded by !LAB.on; the deepest-level record additionally requires G.startLevel===1 so a picked level cannot forge a climb.

name: hop(step)
summary: Changes ring by step, or bumps and still plays a note when there is nowhere to go.
detail: step is -1 outward, +1 inward. Sets G.hopFrom/hopFromI/ringI/hopP, marks the wake, clears nearby red under slipstream, and calls performerHit with the ARRIVING ring. Refuses while a hop is in flight (G.hopP<1).

name: reverse(silent) and reverseFX()
summary: Flips direction immediately and, when silent, defers every effect by REV_FX so a gesture that becomes a swipe can roll it back.
detail: reverse zeroes lapAcc and lapStreak but banks the travelled arc into G.skyW first, so tapping still buys the journey. reverseFX plays the sound, the ripple, the flip and the performer note; commitReverseFX fires it at lift.

name: currentWakeUpdate(dt)
summary: Advances the thirty-six dust strands and decays the shared G.currentFlow envelopes every frame.
detail: Called with the presentation delta from update (7917 for the intro, 8257 for play). It emits new strands only while the reversal is committed (G.revPend<=0), so a speculative tap leaves no wake to roll back. The envelopes it maintains are read by audio, by the shader and by the panner.

name: draw()
summary: The world render pass, in one fixed order, wrapped by runtimeRender's transform repair.
detail: Resets the transform, alpha and composite mode at the top because a thrown frame otherwise poisons every later one. Sets paX/paY (10696) before anything calls posAt. Ends by drawing the HUD and the five controls, with the pause blackout last so it covers them.

name: glRender(dt)
summary: Uploads twenty uniforms and three optional textures, then draws the whole background as one triangle.
detail: Called from draw when GL.on; any throw sets GL.on=false permanently and the CPU sky takes over on the next frame. Its uniforms carry the arena radii, the comet position, the orbit flow envelopes and the starfall progress, which is how the sky answers play rather than a timer.

name: drawBloom()
summary: Rebuilds the bright buffer from every light in the scene and composites the halo, choosing the GPU or the disc path once per frame.
detail: bloomHalo=!FX.on is decided before the dot loop so the two paths can never both draw. The composite resets to setTransform(DPR,...) because the bright pass draws without the camera dolly — the mismatch was a visible wobble on every light.

name: fxRender(srcCanvas,bw,bh)
summary: Blurs the bright buffer at two levels on the GPU and composites them with chromatic spread; returns false on any failure.
detail: Must check isContextLost explicitly: a lost WebGL context does not throw, it silently no-ops, and a quiet success would composite an empty canvas with no way back. A failure is permanent for the session.

name: skyMix()
summary: Interpolates the two neighbouring WORLDS rows into one uniform set, crossfading only over the last 20% of a world.
detail: Reads SKY.w, which skyStep copies from G.skyW. Returns arc, shape, planet, surface, tint, rim, dust, star and motion. Shared by both the GPU and the CPU sky paths so they cannot disagree about where the planet is.

name: scenePulse(kind,duration) and sceneAccent()
summary: Starts at most one authored scene event at a time and reports its current envelope to both the sky and the arena.
detail: scenePulse refuses a duplicate or a lower-ranked kind while one is live, and calls impactRecord so the arena decoration and the sky envelope come from the same event. sceneAccent returns {kind,id,strength,tint} with strength shaped by the event age.

name: drawHUD()
summary: The lesson veil plus the seven-way state dispatch that also publishes every hit rectangle the input handler reads.
detail: Branches: playing (drawRunHUD), lvend, swipesel, menu, levelsel, powersel, else the death screen. There is no paused branch — pause is a flag and the run stays "playing", which is why drawPausePanel is drawn separately after the HUD.

name: hintText()
summary: Returns the one line of standing guidance for right now, or null; each line retires on the action it teaches.
detail: Suppressed entirely outside play, in the intro, in the lab, inside a black hole and during the finale. A live first-encounter lesson outranks it. Every line either quotes MEET or is generated by swipeWords, so the ladder cannot describe a control scheme the build does not have.

name: TIERS
summary: The thirteen-rung unlock ladder: dl threshold, formation type, banner name, lesson sub and optional ring count.
detail: Read by tierIndex, featuredTier, pickType, tierLabel, the ratchet in update and the derived T_VOICE/T_SKY lookups. Rows with type:null announce a ring or the end of teaching and carry no formation. smoke.mjs pins the last rung to the last level's floor.

name: MEET
summary: One sentence and one glyph per teachable idea — the exact string the banner sub and the death coach also print.
detail: Keys are formation types plus orb ids plus orbit, lapcost, music, beat and combo. `soft:1` means the lesson shows without slow motion. Changing a line here means changing its tier row and MECHANICS.md in the same commit.

name: G
summary: The one mutable state object — 75 lines of fields covering clocks, run counters, position, reward states, entities and draw envelopes.
detail: Declared after every function that reads it, and immediately followed by loadPrefs(). G.t is the measured clock and G.vt the presentation clock; G.tsCur is the eased scale between them. G.seen/G.seen2 are the persisted taught sets; G.carry* are the level-boundary handoff.

name: RINGS
summary: Four rows of wave, cutoff multiple, filter lift, sub level and tint — each ring is an instrument.
detail: Read by musicStep (kit stacking), bedTick (the lift term in the pad cutoff), performerHit (the player voice) and the rail draw (the tint). The fourth row is the accretion ring and is only reachable inside a black hole; it is violet because it belongs to the mode, not to the ladder.

name: WORLDS
summary: Eight procedural destinations: position, arc shape, planet placement, surface materials and three colour vectors each.
detail: Order is the journey order and is load-bearing — LEVEL_HOME is a floor against a journey that never goes backwards, so a level home that sits behind an earlier one is dead. Interpolated by skyMix and uploaded as uArc/uShape/uPlanet/uSurface/uTint/uRim/uDust.
